newsitem.title: USA: Exxon settles with insurers over Valdez.
newsitem.headline: Exxon settles with insurers over Valdez.

text.p: Exxon Corp said it has reached a settlement in principle with its insurers regarding claims stemming from the Exxon Valdez oil tanker spill in 1989.

The settlement will result in a final resolution of all matters between Exxon and the insurers, comprised of insurance companies and certain Lloyd's of London syndicates, arising from the Valdez accident, Exxon said.
Under the settlement, insurers have agreed to pay Exxon $480 million to settle the energy company's claims stemming from the Valdez accident.

The settlement represents a final resolution of all matters between Exxon and its insurers arising from the Valdez incident, including Exxon's suit in Texas state court in Houston; an arbitration proceeding between Exxon and the insurers in New York; and a suit by the insurance underwriters against Exxon in federal district court in New York.
Exxon said this settlement comes on top of a $300 million settlement with insurers announced in January for claims arising under a separate section of Exxon's insurance coverage.
The latest settlement brings the total payout from insurers to Exxon to $780 million, Exxon said.
"Exxon is pleased that these claims finally have been resolved," Exxon chairman Lee R. Raymond said. "This settlement will close another chapter of this accident," he said.
A Lloyd's of London spokesman declined to say how much exposure it had to the Valdez accident, but said "certainly Lloyd's had a significant share."
About 167 insurers were involved in the settlement, but Exxon declined to identify the others. However, Exxon said they were based in the U.K., Scandinavia and the United States.
For Lloyd's insurance market, it was one of several heavy blows between 1988 and 1992 that contributed to more than 8.0 billion sterling in losses and almost led to Lloyd's bankruptcy.
